aria: Animated recap of the Timberwolves' 106 to 105 home win over the Trail Blazers: Jaden McDaniels' running layup with 2.6 seconds left, quarter-by-quarter scoring, Ayo Dosunmu's season-high 30 points, the top scorers, how the Timberwolves won, and Thursday's game against the Knicks.
notes: Box score from the Minnesota Timberwolves' 106–105 home win over the Portland Trail Blazers at Target Center on Nov 17, 2026, from the CBS Sports box score and play-by-play, with game details from the Associated Press (via WRAL and KAAL). All 106 Minnesota points and all 105 Portland points are accounted for in the box score, and the quarter scores add up to both totals: Minnesota 29–17 after one, 49–48 Minnesota at the half, 79–79 after three. Team stats (threes 18 of 40 to 16 of 44, field goals 38 of 82 to 38 of 96, blocks 6–4, offensive rebounds 8–14, free throws 12 of 24 to 13 of 20) are from the same box score; bench points (36–44) are summed from its player lines. The biggest leads (Minnesota 12 at 29–17 after the first quarter, Portland 8 at 60–52 in the third after a 12–0 run) are read from the CBS play-by-play. Records and ranks are from the site's standings after Tuesday's games.

Portland led for nearly all of the fourth quarter (AP). Damian Lillard's step-back three made it 102–95 with 1:57 left; LaMelo Ball and Trey Lyles answered with threes, Jrue Holiday hit a three for 105–101, and Ayo Dosunmu's three with 50 seconds left made it 105–104 (CBS play-by-play; AP). Minnesota scored the last five points. Dosunmu's 30 were a season high (AP). Lyles blocked Lillard's last shot with one second left (AP; CBS play-by-play). Rudy Gobert was scoreless for the first time this season, in foul trouble in the first half (AP). Minnesota missed 12 free throws (AP; box score). Deni Avdija (sore foot) sat out for Portland and Jonathan Kuminga (right shoulder contusion) for Minnesota (AP). Minnesota also beat Portland 106–98 on Monday (AP). The Timberwolves host the Knicks on Thursday (AP).

The play of the game is an original illustration of Jaden McDaniels' running layup with 2.6 seconds left (AP gives 2.6 seconds; the CBS play-by-play logs it at 0:02 as a running layup assisted by Ayo Dosunmu, right after a Donovan Clingan bad pass stolen by LaMelo Ball, with the score going from 105–104 Portland to 106–105 Minnesota). The AP says Minnesota stole Portland's inbounds pass. The recaps don't describe the drive itself, so it is drawn as a plain drive to a short finish. The figures are stylized and not traced from footage, and the spacing is not to scale.

The music is an original beat made for this page. No existing recordings or melodies are used. This is an unofficial fan recap, not affiliated with the Minnesota Timberwolves or the NBA, which is why it carries a plain basketball mark and the team's colors but not the team's logo.

The player in the play of the game is drawn to McDaniels' listed 6-foot-9 and 185 pounds (RealGM; Wikipedia), with arms scaled to his reported 7-foot wingspan (Sportskeeda), in Minnesota's home white with No. 3 (RealGM; Wikipedia). He has no approved look on file yet, so he is drawn in the kit with the default skin tone. It is an original figure with a featureless face, not a portrait or a trace of footage.
